tldr: This is a loose cluster of three unrelated projects that share one goal: serving LLMs faster below the model layer. It began with Resin, a native scheduler for inference engines, and was followed by Hibana, an arXiv paper on agentic inference for unified-memory devices.
whats_new: Warmctl, a new open-source tool shared on Show HN, targets slow cold starts for vLLM servers, adding a startup-latency fix to a thread about scheduling and local serving.
why_it_matters: Inference latency increasingly depends on the layers around the model (request scheduling, memory layout, server warm-up), and each of these projects targets one of those layers.

beats.headline: Resin: a native scheduler for LLM inference engines
beats.summary: A Show HN project that puts request scheduling into a native component sitting in front of the inference engine.

beats.headline: Hibana targets agentic inference on unified-memory devices
beats.summary: Research on running agent workloads such as coding with open-weight models on local hardware with shared CPU/GPU memory.

beats.headline: Warmctl tackles vLLM cold starts
beats.summary: A Show HN tool aimed at the startup delay before a vLLM server can take traffic.

open_questions: Does Warmctl publish cold-start timings against a stock vLLM startup on named models and GPUs?
Does Resin integrate with vLLM or SGLang, or does it require its own engine?
Does Hibana release code, and which unified-memory hardware does it benchmark on?
take_for_builders: If vLLM startup time limits your autoscaling, measure your current cold-start time first, then trial Warmctl on a non-production replica and compare.

day_captions.a38548abbeed9a82: Moves the thread from servers to local devices, with a research take on agent workloads.
day_captions.131509a7651f4930: Adds cold-start latency as a separate bottleneck, specific to vLLM deployments.
